newsitem.title: FRANCE: BOE's Davies says 96 growth of 2.3-2.5 pct likely.
newsitem.headline: BOE's Davies says 96 growth of 2.3-2.5 pct likely.

text.p: Bank of England Deputy Governor Howard Davies said on Friday it was looking more likely the pace of economic growth in the U.K. in 1996 would be between 2.3 and 2.5 percent.
Speaking to reporters in Paris, Davies said, "It's not certain we'll reach that rate, but it's likely. It's becoming more and more likely."
Although Davies said the U.K. economy had a higher growth rate than elsewhere in Europe, it still had a problem with its budget deficit which was too high.
"The government is forecasting a figure of about three percent (as a percentage of GDP) in 1997 but at the moment we don't know how that's going to happen," Davies said.
He also said the pound was relatively stable and for now there did not appear to be an pressure on the currency.
